description: Count the track elements in a GPX file with the GPX Track Count Tool — multi-day and multi-activity files audited locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a file exported from a week-long tour often holds 7 tracks — one per day — and this counter is how you confirm the export kept every day before you archive the originals.
quick_answer: The GPX Track Count Tool counts the <trk> elements in a GPX file — each track being one recorded activity or one day of a multi-day export. Drop the file and read the track count locally, so multi-activity files can be audited before they are split, merged or archived.

body.t: A runner pauses twice at water stops: the file holds 1 <trk> with 3 <trkseg> elements. Segments record pauses; tracks record activities. This counter counts activities — 1 — and the example is why users think their file 'lost' tracks it never had.

faq: The headline number is tracks. Segments matter for pause analysis, and the distinction is explained in the table on this page — most 'missing track' puzzles are segment-versus-track confusion.
Can a file have zero tracks?
Yes — a waypoints-only or route-only GPX is valid and reports zero tracks. That is information, not an error.
My app exported one track per day. Is that normal?
Very — multi-activity devices and tour planners export exactly that way. The count confirms each day survived the export.
An empty <trk> shell occasionally survives sloppy exports. It still counts as a track element — structural counting is literal.
What if the file is actually a TCX or FIT?
Those are different formats (FIT is binary) and will not parse as GPX. Convert at the source app first.
Track <name> elements (often the activity title or date) are how you identify which track is which after counting — the viewer displays them on the map.
